plugins.name: mcp-diagnostics
plugins.description: Diagnose MCP servers that run but expose no tools, config changes that never take effect, and token blowups from oversized tool returns.

plugins.name: component-upgrade
plugins.description: Plan and execute version upgrades of self-hosted components -- Docker containers, databases, and git-deployed services -- with a restore-verified backup, an execution-driven config-migration check, and a tested rollback path.

plugins.name: deep-research
plugins.description: Route a research or diagnosis request to the right scenario, drill at least three layers deep, then summarize and verify the conclusion -- including the ten traps that make a half-finished investigation look complete.

plugins.name: component-lifecycle
plugins.description: The gap after 'the component is installed': container and systemd lifecycle, layered fault isolation, multi-point verification, state snapshots, and the integration checklist -- plus the cron no_agent script-path pitfall.

plugins.name: integration-verification
plugins.description: Prove an integration actually took effect instead of looking configured: the silently-failing three-variable env trap, a preflight check that passes while the real path is broken, and a credential display mask that produces an auth failure with zero logs.

plugins.name: clickhouse-operations
plugins.description: Operating a self-hosted ClickHouse behind another service: system-log TTL governance when XML config and the engine definition disagree, repairing key-column values, corrupted-parts triage, verified backup/restore, and trace timestamps that drift by whole hours.

plugins.name: verify-conclusion
plugins.description: Stress-test a diagnostic conclusion before acting on it: classify every link as fact, assumption, or inference, blind re-derive with a different reasoning strategy, and catch the fifteen real traps that make a plausible conclusion wrong.

plugins.name: browser-site-driving
plugins.description: Drive a real website with a browser when the page fights back: WSL headless-Chromium setup, the desktop-UA disguise that defeats a mobile-only interception page, DOM forensics instead of screenshots, static SPA-bundle reconnaissance before login, proving login persistence from the cookie database, and a plan/execute/re-check loop for reproducing an object on a platform whose UI offers no clone feature.
